# DTE — Data Transformation Engine for Apache Airflow

> DTE is an open-source (Apache-2.0, beta) batch data transformation engine
> that runs as an Apache Airflow 3 plugin. Map a source once in a visual
> pipeline builder; every pipeline becomes an Airflow DAG that Airflow
> schedules, runs and records.

## What it does

- **Runs inside Airflow 3.3+**, installed with pip into an existing deployment: the UI is a native Airflow `react_apps` plugin,
  each pipeline is a `dte__<id>` DAG, and Airflow owns login, connections,
  scheduling and run history.
- **Sources**: local files (JSON/JSONL/CSV/Parquet/Excel), Amazon S3, Google
  Cloud Storage, Azure Blob / ADLS, SFTP, Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite, Snowflake,
  BigQuery, MongoDB, REST APIs (paginated), PDF documents.
- **Transform steps**: filter, rename, retype, map/lookup, map/expression, sort,
  aggregate, join, pivot, select/drop fields, PDF extract and structure.
- **Data quality**: check (assert a SQL rule, fail or warn), profile (null %,
  distinct count, min/max), and a dry-run preview before every run.
- **Destinations**: Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, and
  Parquet/JSON/CSV/Excel files locally or on S3, GCS, Azure or SFTP.
- **Connections**: Airflow connections. Whatever Airflow provider is installed
  (amazon, google, microsoft-azure, sftp, postgres, mysql, mssql, snowflake,
  mongo, http), DTE supports that connection; the provider does the auth.
- Engine: DuckDB + ibis, with dlt loaders.

## Quickstart

Into an existing Airflow 3.3+, with Airflow's constraints file unmodified:

    curl -fsSLo constraints.txt https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apache/airflow/constraints-3.3.2/constraints-3.12.txt
    pip install dte-airflow --constraint constraints.txt
    export DTE_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@host/dte   # DTE's own database
    dte db upgrade

Add the one-line DAG file (`from dte.airflow.dag_factory import build_dags;
globals().update(build_dags())`), restart Airflow; DTE is under Plugins ▸ DTE
Pipelines. Guide: https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/self-hosting/install-plugin

## Docs

Full docs as one Markdown file: https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/llms-full.txt
Docs index for LLMs: https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/llms.txt

- [Install into your own Airflow](https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/self-hosting/install-plugin): pip install into Airflow 3.3+, database setup, the DAG file
- [Try it with Docker Compose](https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/self-hosting/install): a full local stack in one command
- [Your first pipeline](https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/getting-started/02-first-pipeline): source to destination, step by step
- [Core ideas](https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/getting-started/03-concepts): pipelines, steps, field names, runs
- [Steps](https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/steps/): every transform and quality step
- [Sources](https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/sources/) and [Destinations](https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/destinations/): what DTE reads and writes
- [Connections](https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/connections/): how DTE uses Airflow connections
- [Scheduling](https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/pipelines/scheduling), [Preview & run](https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/pipelines/preview-and-run)
- [Architecture overview](https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/architecture/overview)
- [FAQ](https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/faq), [Troubleshooting](https://dte.flowexperts.ai/docs/troubleshooting)
